articles.title: Apple bundles TV, Arcade with iCloud+; ends standalone Apple One subscriptions in India
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional co.
articles.body: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost, combining cloud storage, video streaming and gaming in a single subscription.Apple is also introducing Apple Select, a new service integrated into the existing Apple Music app, exclusively for iCloud+ subscribers. This addition extends the expanded bundle’s benefits to the music app, offering subscribers an exclusive collection of music.The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Subscribers can share the package with up to five family members. The rollout will take place through September.The change will end standalone Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions sold directly by Apple in India. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+. Apple said access would remain uninterrupted and Arcade game progress and saves would be preserved.Apple One, which bundles several Apple services, will also close to new subscribers in India. Existing subscribers will retain their subscriptions. This means new customers seeking Apple’s combined storage and entertainment offering will be directed towards iCloud+, while current Apple One users can continue with their existing package.Apple One currently has two plans in India: Individual at Rs 195 a month, with 50GB of iCloud+ storage, and Family at Rs 365 a month, with 200GB, shareable with up to five other family members. Both include Apple Music, Apple TV and Apple Arcade. Apple Music is not included in the newly announced iCloud+ bundle, a key distinction for users comparing the offerings.The shift turns cloud storage, often bought when free space runs out, into an entry point for Apple’s entertainment services. For existing iCloud+ customers, the immediate benefit is access to streaming and games without an additional subscription bill.For Apple, bundling could help expose more paying customers to services they may not have chosen separately. It also gives users another reason to retain their storage subscription. However, customers who want only Apple TV or Arcade will now have to take the combined offering when subscribing directly through Apple.“We’re excited to bring Apple TV and Apple Arcade to iCloud+ users in over 100 countries in one convenient subscription,” said Eddy Cue, Apple’s senior vice president of Services and Health.Airtel customers with iPhones can also access the expanded subscription through eligible postpaid plans. Those already receiving Apple TV through select Airtel plans can transition at no additional cost. Availability of individual features, shows and games may vary by country, region or device.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: In 1998, 31 Przewalski’s horses were brought to Chernobyl; deaths and poaching followed before their numbers reached 137 by 2018
articles.summary: Rest of World News: When the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone was abandoned after the 1986 nuclear disaster, it was not expected to become part of the future of a horse that had .
articles.body: When the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone was abandoned after the 1986 nuclear disaster, it was not expected to become part of the future of a horse that had already vanished from the wild. Yet, more than a decade later, Przewalski’s horses were brought into the largely empty landscape in an effort to establish a free-ranging population. According to the study published in Theriologia Ukrainica, titled ‘Przewalski`s horse (Equus ferus przewalskii) in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone after 20 years of introduction’ claim that 31 horses were released in 1998 and multiplied. The records tell a more complicated story. The animals arrived over two years, some died before joining the wild population, and poaching caused serious losses during the first decade. Even so, the horses continued breeding. By 2018, 137 had been documented in Ukraine, with others across the Belarusian border.How Przewalski’s horses were introduced to the Chernobyl Exclusion ZoneThe introduction began in 1998 and continued into 1999. Twenty-eight Przewalski’s horses came from the Askania Nova Biosphere Reserve, made up of 10 males and 18 females. Three more males were brought from the zoo at the Lozovski stud-farm.That is the origin of the familiar total of 31, although saying that all 31 became the founders of Chernobyl's free-ranging population leaves out what happened next, as reported by Chernobyl, Pripyat, Chernobyl Exclusion Zone.Eight animals died during transport or shortly afterwards, with injury and stress among the recorded problems. Those that survived were not immediately turned loose. They spent anything from several weeks to eight months in large enclosures while they acclimatised.When the early history of the population was later examined, the animals identified as successful reproductive founders were a much smaller group: two stallions and 15 mares from Askania Nova. The purpose of the project was also broader than simply putting an endangered animal into an abandoned radioactive area. The plan was to create a free-ranging population while increasing biodiversity and helping restore ecological processes in a landscape that had been heavily altered by human activity before the disaster.The uncertain history behind Przewalski’s horsesPrzewalski’s horses had disappeared from the wild during the twentieth century. Their survival depended on captive breeding programmes, from which later reintroduction projects were developed.The species has often been described as the world's last truly wild horse, sometimes with the added claim that it was never domesticated. That description has become less straightforward as archaeological evidence has been re-examined.A reassessment published in Scientific Reports in 2021, titled 'Rethinking the evidence for early horse domestication at Botai’ looked again at evidence from Botai in Kazakhstan, a site long associated with early horse domestication. The authors argued that the remains could instead reflect large-scale hunting of wild Przewalski’s horses. Their interpretation did not settle every question about the species' past relationship with people, but it made the old certainty harder to maintain. For Chernobyl, the more immediate fact was simpler. A horse that had survived only through captive populations was being given space to live and breed freely again.Przewalski’s horses grew in number but faced early lossesOnce breeding began, numbers increased quickly. The population reached 65 animals in both 2003 and 2004. That growth did not continue without interruption. By 2007, the number had fallen to around 50. At the end of the following year, 64 horses were counted.Illegal hunting was part of the problem, although the surviving records do not allow every loss to be assigned a cause. Between 1999 and 2006, 55 free-ranging horses were lost. A cause of death could only be determined in 18 cases, and 13 of those deaths were attributed to poaching.The early study therefore found that poaching accounted for more than 70 per cent of the deaths for which a cause was known. It could not say the same about all 55 losses. The horses were reproducing and establishing themselves, but the population was also vulnerable to pressures that could not always be measured clearly from the available records.Chernobyl’s Przewalski’s horses were no longer just scattered survivorsA more detailed picture emerged from camera-trap work carried out in 2018. In the Ukrainian part of the exclusion zone, 137 Przewalski’s horses were recorded. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the count included 47 stallions, 66 adult mares and fillies, and 24 foals. Beyond the Ukrainian survey area, at least four more animals were recorded at a remote site in the Belarusian exclusion zone: one stallion, two mares and a foal.These were not simply scattered individuals moving randomly through the landscape. The survey recorded 13 harem groups containing foals, along with four small groups that were not breeding, around six groups of stallions and at least one solitary male.Some of the horses were using territory on both sides of the international border.Their presence in Belarus had developed over several years. Horses were reported crossing the Prypiat River between 2007 and 2010, after which a breeding subpopulation became established there. By the time of the 2018 survey, the original introduction was already becoming part of the population's distant history. Almost every horse recorded belonged to the second generation or a later one. Only two mares still carried brands linking them directly to the animals brought into the zone at the end of the 1990s.Chernobyl’s wild horses adapted to a landscape far beyond open meadowsPrzewalski’s horses are usually associated with open country, and meadows remained an important part of their habitat in Chernobyl. The 2018 survey, though, showed that the animals were not avoiding forested areas. That is significant because the exclusion zone is far from an open grassland. Woodland and reforested ground cover large areas, and the changing landscape has also made it harder to count animals by direct observation.The horses were using a broader range of habitat than a simple steppe image might suggest. Their movements through forests also help explain why camera traps and repeated field observations became important for understanding how the population was distributed.Population growth cannot answer every question about radiationThe presence of a growing Przewalski’s horse population in Chernobyl does not mean that radiation has no biological effects. Population numbers and the health of individual animals are different questions. A population can grow while some animals experience effects that are not visible in a basic count. At the same time, many pressures disappeared or were greatly reduced when people left the area after the disaster.Farming, traffic, development and regular human disturbance were no longer shaping the landscape in the same way. Those changes created conditions that cannot easily be separated from radiation exposure when looking only at the population's overall increase.The 2018 work was concerned with where the horses lived, how they were organised socially and how the population had developed over time. It was not a controlled experiment designed to isolate radiation as a single variable.Its results show that the horses reproduced successfully and remained established in the exclusion zone. They do not establish that radiation is harmless, nor do they identify one factor as the explanation for the population's survival.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From TVs to refrigerators: What Amazon's survey reveals about how India shops for appliances
articles.summary: Tech News News: Amazon India has released the third set of findings from its inaugural Best in Tech Survey, revealing how Indian consumers choose Smart TVs and home a.
articles.body: Amazon India has released the third set of findings from its inaugural Best in Tech Survey, revealing how Indian consumers choose Smart TVs and home appliances. Picture quality emerged as the leading feature preference for Smart TV buyers, while energy star rating ranked highest for air conditioner and refrigerator buyers. Flexible financing also plays a decisive role, with nearly half of large appliance buyers citing No-Cost EMI as the most important pricing lever.A data-driven look at what India wantsThe survey, drawn from more than 40,000 responses across major consumer electronics categories, is part of an ongoing Amazon India initiative to understand what shapes tech purchase decisions on its platform. This latest release covers Smart TVs, air conditioners, refrigerators, and washing machines, and its findings will help shape both product selection on Amazon.in and the upcoming second edition of the Best in Tech Awards, scheduled for September 18, 2026.Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India, said the findings reinforce a pattern seen in the survey's earlier rounds on personal devices, now extending into home appliances as well: brand trust remains foundational, but customers are researching extensively and expecting a consistently high standard across the entire buying journey, from product page to installation. She noted that AI has moved well beyond smartphones and laptops and is now becoming a meaningful part of how people think about home appliances too.Smart TVs: Picture quality rules, AI interest varies by budgetPicture quality emerged as the single most important purchase factor for Smart TV buyers, cited by 66% of respondents. At higher price points above ₹60,000, buyers are gravitating toward OLED and Mini LED/Neo QLED panels, with Mini LED emerging as a strong contender at the premium end. Financing also plays a major role: two-thirds of buyers said EMI or "buy now, pay later" options influence their decision, with EMI mattering to 36% of buyers under Rs 25,000, 40% in the Rs 25,000–Rs 60,000 range, and 38% above that threshold.Preference for premium display technology has also become remarkably consistent nationwide, with roughly 8 in 10 buyers favoring QLED, OLED, or Mini LED/Neo QLED panels across metros as well as Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, leaving basic LED TVs a small minority almost everywhere.AI-powered features are generating real excitement, with 60% of Smart TV buyers saying they're drawn to them — though what "AI" means to buyers shifts with budget.Buyers spending above ₹60,000 are mainly interested in AI-powered picture enhancement, cited by 51% of premium buyers, while those under ₹25,000 lean toward voice assistants, cited by 39% in that segment. Movies and OTT content remain the top overall reason to buy a Smart TV, followed by family entertainment, while gaming shows particular strength in Tier 2 cities. Installation also directly shapes purchase decisions for over a third of buyers, reflecting an expectation that the experience doesn't end at checkout.Air conditioners: Energy efficiency and transparent installation matter mostFor AC buyers, a high energy star rating is the top priority, cited by 35% of respondents, ahead of inverter technology (24%) and convertible cooling (21%) — suggesting energy efficiency itself, rather than the specific underlying technology, has become the primary filter buyers apply. On the service side, nearly half of AC buyers said free installation with no hidden charges is their top expectation, followed by trained and certified technicians (20%) and combined delivery-and-installation in a single visit (17%).Refrigerators: Delivery experience is the deciding factorRefrigerator buyers put an unusually strong emphasis on delivery quality: seven in ten said damage-free delivery with full packaging inspection is their top expectation, well ahead of old-refrigerator exchange or removal (16%) and exact placement within the kitchen (9%). On the product side, energy star rating again topped the list of desired features at 30%, followed by convertible modes (25%) and inverter compressors (22%). When it comes to what would justify spending beyond a planned budget, 28% pointed to a significantly higher energy rating with provable long-term savings, another 28% cited genuinely useful convertible technology, and 18% said longer warranty periods would justify paying more.Washing machines: Inverter motors lead, AI wash programs gaining groundWashing machine buyers ranked inverter motors as their top feature, cited by 40% of respondents for their combination of quiet operation, energy savings, and durability. AI-powered wash programs that automatically detect fabric type and load size are emerging as a fast-rising second choice at 18%, suggesting smart laundry features are shifting from a premium extra to a mainstream expectation. Nearly half of buyers said delivery and installation need to happen in a single visit, with professional plumbing setup the second most commonly cited need at 20%.This installment builds on two earlier rounds of the Best in Tech Survey. The first found that AI features now influence purchase decisions for 82% of smartphone buyers on Amazon.in, while the second found processor performance to be the top driver for laptop buyers at 87%, with AI enthusiasm running highest in the computing category. Across all three rounds, a consistent theme has emerged: Indian buyers are evaluating tech and appliance purchases on detailed specifications, prioritizing efficiency and long-term value, and expecting the post-purchase experience — delivery, installation, and setup — to match the quality of the product itself.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Does India still need Russia’s S-500? How its own missile shield is changing the equation
articles.summary: News News: Recent and ongoing conflicts have demonstrated the requirement for a comprehensive and layered air defence environment. Modern air defences are tasked.
articles.body: Recent and ongoing conflicts have demonstrated the requirement for a comprehensive and layered air defence environment. Modern air defences are tasked with defending against everything from the off the shelf drone to ballistic missiles and everything in between. During the active phase of Operation Sindoor, India defended against almost the entire spectrum of aerial threats ranging from small Pakistani drones to ballistic missiles. Even, well over a year, the Pakistanis have not been able to provide proof of their strikes, instead resorting to AI generated videos on their National Defence Day earlier this month.During the active phase of the operation in May last year, the Pakistanis fired a Fatah series of ballistic missile that wad intercepted over Sirsa in Haryana by the air force. Hunting ballistic missiles is one of the most complex tasks and requires the precise working of different types of systems ranging from the early warning radar to the acquisition radar that relays information to the firing unit and at the end the interceptor that has to connect with a projectile hurtling towards the earth at hypersonic speeds. The devastation caused by these weapons has been on display with the Iranians and their proxies the Houthis terrorising the region with these weapons.To tackle this problem, the Russians have developed the S-500 Prometheus system. This weapons complex armed with missiles such as the 77N6 and a variant of this missile named the 77N6-N1 which can take out ballistic missiles at ranges of up to 600 km at altitudes of up to 200 km. According to Washington DC based think tank, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), this missile is also capable of taking out Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. Unlike the S-400, which offers theatre-level protection out to 400 kilometres against aircraft, drones and cruise missiles, the S-500 Prometheus is not designed to replace the S-400, but to supplement it. With the S-400 being more adept at taking down aircraft, drones and cruise missiles, this leaves open other threats such as ballistic missiles and hypersonic weapons. The Russians have been pitching the S-500 to India since 2021.This comes at a time when India is developing its own Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD) apparatus. The country has taken a major leap in its missile defence capability, successfully completing the final development trials of Phase-II of its Ballistic Missile Defence shield. Conducted by DRDO on June 10-11 using the AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors, the tests validated India's ability to intercept incoming ballistic missiles both inside and outside the atmosphere, placing the country in a select group of nations capable of defending against ICBM-class threats.The system is designed to counter some of the most challenging targets in modern warfare, hypersonic weapons, manoeuvring glide vehicles, and missiles fitted with MIRV technology that can release multiple warheads toward different targets simultaneously. This layered shield relies on a network of launch vehicles, long-range radars, Launch Control Centres and a central Mission Control Centre, all linked through a secure communication system.While Phase-I already offers limited operational protection to Delhi and Mumbai against threats up to 2,000 kilometres, Phase-II extends that umbrella dramatically, to missiles with ranges approaching 5,000 kilometres. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh described the tests as validating the critical technologies underpinning India's broader multi-layered defence shield.Mobility is central to the new system too, with indigenous 12x12 Transporter-Erector-Launchers, built by Ashok Leyland and integrated by DRDO and Tata Advanced Systems, giving the AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors genuine shoot-and-scoot capability across difficult terrain. With the domestic BMD system maturing under the overall ambit of Project Kusha, the space for a foreign weapons project could perhaps be reducing.

articles.title: 'Distressing': BJP slams Congress over three of its CMs 'skipping' Brics dinner
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday slammed Congress after three of its chief ministers skipped the dinner for Brics leaders hosted by the go.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday slammed Congress after three of its chief ministers skipped the dinner for Brics leaders hosted by the government, accusing them of "prioritising partisan politics over the national interest."At a press conference, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj asked Congress whether, in opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it had begun opposing India as well."Political and ideological differences can always exist in politics. But when it comes to India and national interest, there should be no room for personal animosity or discord," Bansuri said."It is distressing that when the three chief ministers from the Congress party were invited to the Brics summit dinner, they prioritised partisan politics over the national interest .... I would like to ask Congress - in your opposition to PM Modi, have you now started to oppose India as well?" she added.BJP MP's remarks came after official sources said that CMs hailing from opposition parties were also invited for Brics dinner but did not attend the event.While Tamil Nadu CM Vijay was abroad, three Congress CMs invited for the dinner chose to skip it.A day before the dinner on September 12, Telangana CM Revanth Reddy had accepted the invitation for the dinner hosted by PM Modi. However, Reddy's office later conveyed to govt that he would be unable to attend due to "unavoidable circumstances".Two other Congress chief ministers, V D Satheesan of Kerala and D K Shivakumar of Karnataka, also skipped the dinner.The decision to invite CMs of different states for the dinner for BRICS leaders was in keeping with govt's move to host numerous events related to the grouping during India's presidency across various cities, and the decision of opposition CMs to skip it was unfortunate, the sources said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘29 Sept tak metro mein safar na karein’: Multiple Delhi schools receive bomb threats
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Several schools in Delhi received bomb threats via email on Tuesday, prompting security checks and searches across the affected premises.Th.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Several schools in Delhi received bomb threats via email on Tuesday, prompting security checks and searches across the affected premises.The threat email, reportedly sent in Punjabi, claimed that blasts would target courts and police stations in the national capital.The threat emails were received at around 10:17 am. The schools named among those affected include Air Force Bal Bharati School (AFBBS), Carmel Convent School and The British School.One of the threat emails carried the subject line: “B00000M|B New Dellhi Schools @ 1:11PM.”The email contained threatening messages, including: “Delhi BanayGa KHALISTAN” and “School @1:11pm Delhi valio Apne Bachay Bachao Koi ve Metro Yan Traina Vich 29 Sept Tak Safar na Karna, Delhi da har police thana Nishana iPhone Dhamake hon Ge.”The email further threatened court premises, stating: “Court @3:11pm Tees Hazari, Karkardoma Court, Patila Court Khalistan vale Sikhan Nu jhoothe case Saja karde - Ajj ton courtan te parkng Vich Lagatar Scooterian Nal Dhamake.”It also warned: “Delhi da har police chowkian Nishane te,” according to the email.Following the threats, a major security operation was launched at the affected schools. Delhi Police deployed bomb disposal squads and sniffer dog units to conduct thorough searches of the premises.Multiple fire tenders and ambulances were kept on standby as a precautionary measure. Sniffer dogs searched classrooms, corridors and open areas, while personnel from the bomb detection and disposal squads scanned the premises using specialised equipment for any possible explosive devices.Local police personnel were also deployed to manage crowds of concerned parents and maintain security around the schools.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: In the 1940s, common ragweed spread with American agricultural aid meant to rebuild Japan, but it became widespread across roadsides, fields, and cities nationwide and contributed to seasonal hay fever
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Explore the unexpected arrival of common ragweed in Japan post-World War II, its spread across the nation, and its significant impact on public health, triggering a hay fever epidemic that persists to this day.
articles.body: Massive amounts of food, seed, and raw materials must be transported across borders to rebuild a nation following a catastrophic conflict, typically with significantly more hurry than caution. The United States provided Japan with this kind of extensive assistance in the years following World War II in the form of wheat, animal feed, and other agricultural supplies meant to avert widespread hunger and revive Japanese agriculture. Among the plants that later benefited from increased movement of agricultural goods was common ragweed, Ambrosia artemisiifolia, a North American species capable of thriving in disturbed ground. Japan's experience would eventually turn the plant from a minor introduction into a widespread source of seasonal pollen.An old arrival that spread after conditions changedCommon ragweed had reached Japan decades before the war, with the first record dating to around 1877. Japan's National Institute for Environmental Studies lists the species as an introduced plant that later established itself in the wild. For decades, it remained a relatively limited introduction rather than a nationwide presence.What changed after 1945 was the scale of disturbance and the movement of goods. Bomb-damaged urban areas, cleared building sites, expanding farmland and newly disturbed roadsides created the kind of open ground on which ragweed could thrive. Increased movement of agricultural commodities also provided opportunities for seeds to travel. The species eventually became widespread across Japan, occurring in farmland, orchards, pastures, roadsides, vacant lots, woodland edges and riverbanks.From nuisance on the roadside to established allergiesJapan's recognition of pollen allergy developed gradually. A systematic study of pollinosis carried out in 1960–61 included a patient with ragweed pollinosis, providing an early documented example of pollen-related allergy in the country. Japanese cedar pollinosis was identified separately after doctors in Nikko investigated patients with recurring spring symptoms in 1963, with the first report published in 1964.Cedar and cypress pollen dominate Japan's spring allergy season, while ragweed releases its pollen in late summer and early autumn, creating a later period of seasonal exposure, which releases its pollen in late summer and early fall, providing Japan a second, lesser wave of seasonal allergy sufferers each year. In urban Saitama, airborne pollen surveys found ragweed pollen levels exceeded the level associated with the onset of clinical allergy symptoms for approximately six weeks in early autumn, and on some days pollen levels were so high that they posed a risk of triggering asthma-related emergency visits.A plant no one has learnt to weed outCommon ragweed remains widespread in Japan and is recognized as an invasive alien species. The National Institute for Environmental Studies lists competition with native plants among its ecological effects, while the species is also important from a public-health perspective because its pollen can trigger seasonal allergic reactions.Research on common ragweed in other regions has similarly linked its spread to international grain trade and transportation networks. A recent study of East China, for example, identified multiple introductions and found that modern grain trade between the United States and China was a major invasion pathway. Ragweed can spread through trade and transportation before becoming established in disturbed habitats. Japan's history with the plant illustrates how an introduction recorded in the 19th century can expand over subsequent decades and eventually become both an ecological and public-health concern. Japan’s postwar experience, driven by an emergency to feed the population, left it with a seasonal health annoyance that outlasted the crisis that birthed it by many decades.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Bhagne nahi dunga kisi ko’: Gangster Himanshu Bhau claims responsibility for Delhi gym trainer murder
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Gangster Himanshu Bhau has claimed responsibility for the murder of a 30-year-old gym trainer in south Delhi’s Fatehpur Beri, with police v.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Gangster Himanshu Bhau has claimed responsibility for the murder of a 30-year-old gym trainer in south Delhi’s Fatehpur Beri, with police verifying the authenticity of the social media post attributed to the gangster and probing whether the claim is linked to the killing.In a later post, purportedly by Bhau, the gangster issued a warning in Hindi, saying, “Bhagne se kam nahi chalega field me aao. Bhagne nahi dunga kisi ko (Running away won't help, come out to the field. I won't let anyone run away).” The post mentioned “Bhau gang” and “Since-2020”, the post read.The victim, Vijay Lohia of Fatehpur Beri, was shot dead after bike-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at him near Hansa Chowk around 10am on Monday. Police suspect the attack may be linked to an old rivalry between two families that has already claimed two lives.No arrest has been made so far. Deputy commissioner of police (south) Anant Mittal said a team rushed to the spot after receiving information about the firing. “Several rounds were fired by two suspects, resulting in one person sustaining fatal injuries and subsequently succumbing,” he said.According to police, an FIR was registered under BNS Section 103 (murder) at Fatehpuri Beri police station against unknown persons. Raids are being conducted to trace the suspects and teams have been formed to arrest them, Mittal said.Sources said the assailants were waiting outside the gym for Vijay. While some sources said four men were involved, police said only two men carried out the attack. The suspects were wearing helmets and were riding two motorcycles that allegedly had fake numberplates, a source said. “It appears they had been conducting reconnaissance for the past few days,” the source added.Vijay was called outside the gym on the pretext that someone wanted to speak to him. He was ambushed as soon as he stepped out, with the assailants allegedly firing around 12-15 rounds. Vijay suffered multiple injuries, including at least two to the head. He was taken to a hospital, where he was declared dead.Vijay is survived by his wife, Ritu, 24.Police are also verifying the authenticity of the social media post attributed to Bhau, who is based abroad, and investigating whether the claim has any connection with the killing.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 'Umar Khalid is a nationalist': Congress leader BK Hariprasad hits out at ABVP amid documentary row
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Karnataka Congress president BK Hariprasad on Tuesday hit out at the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) over its demand for the perm.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Karnataka Congress president BK Hariprasad on Tuesday hit out at the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) over its demand for the permanent cancellation of a proposed documentary screening on jailed activist Umar Khalid at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU). Hariprasad called Khalid a nationalist and questioned the student organisation's moral authority to comment on him.Hariprasad said, "Umar Khalid is a nationalist, and ABVP has no right to speak on him because they adore Nathuram Godse—who was an anti-national and the first terrorist of the country. They have no moral right."The remarks came after the RSS-affiliated student organisation sought the Centre's intervention to permanently cancel the proposed screening of the documentary Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, directed by Lalit Vachani, at NLSIU.The screening was recently postponed by the organisers, who cited security and administrative reasons.In a statement on Monday, ABVP Bengaluru claimed it had sent representations to Union home minister Amit Shah, Union education minister Pralhad Joshi and Union minister of state (independent charge) for law and justice Arjun Ram Meghwal, seeking their intervention.The organisation also called for a high-level inquiry into the NLSIU administration over the proposed event.ABVP alleged that the postponement was a "stalling tactic" intended to allow public outrage to subside. It said institutions of national repute should not become platforms for what it described as political propaganda centred on Khalid.The student body referred to Khalid's alleged links to the 2016 JNU controversy, Afzal Guru commemorations, CAA-NRC protests and the 2020 Delhi riots.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1930, St Kilda’s last residents evacuated the Scottish islands; within 18 months, its house mice vanished while larger field mice moved into abandoned homes
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 1930, the evacuation of human residents from Scotland’s St Kilda islands led to the extinction of the St Kilda house mouse while the field mouse thrived in the abandoned habitats. This article explores the ecological impact of human departure and the fate of two mouse populations.
articles.body: The last residents of St Kilda left the remote Scottish archipelago in 1930, bringing an end to a human community that had survived on the islands for generations. The departure’s impact went far beyond the social history of the isolated settlement. Within around 18 months, the St Kilda house mouse, a population that was closely associated with human habitation, became extinct. On the other hand, the islands’ already-established field mice expanded into abandoned buildings that were previously occupied almost exclusively by house mice.About 66 kilometres west of Benbecula in Scotland’s Outer Hebrides lies St Kilda. Its largest island, Hirta, was the centre of the permanent settlement, and by the beginning of 1930, only 36 people remained there, according to the National Records of Scotland. They lived in 10 households, while six of the island’s 16 rented cottages were already empty. Sheep rearing, fishing and the harvesting of seabird resources, which were considered traditional livelihoods, had become increasingly difficult to sustain. In addition to this, sometimes bad weather would interrupt deliveries of food and mail.The evacuation that followed was therefore not a part of a response to an ecological experiment. Instead, after a particularly difficult winter in 1929–30, the remaining residents decided that staying on the island was no longer viable. Archived records suggest that the residents requested evacuation, and that on 29 August 1930 the remaining community left for the Scottish mainland. This departure unintentionally impacted the conditions under which two different mouse populations had lived alongside one another.With the departure of humans, house mice lost their human-made habitatSt Kilda had two distinctive mouse populations. One was the St Kilda house mouse, Mus musculus muralis, a form of mouse associated with the island’s human settlement, and the other was the St Kilda field mouse, Apodemus sylvaticus hirtensis, a subspecies of wood mouse that survived in the island’s natural environment. Despite being island forms, both populations’ relationships with human habitation were different. According to the National Trust for Scotland, the St Kilda house mouse became extinct after the 1930 evacuation, while the field mouse remains common on Hirta and is also found on Dun.Conditions created by a permanent human population had greatly benefited the house mice. The houses provided shelter, while food stored by the humans offered a dependable resource for them. On the other hand, field mice were already established on the island but were less closely associated with human buildings. Therefore, when people disappeared from the island, the change was not that a new species suddenly arrived. Instead, the balance between the two populations changed drastically because one species lost the environment they were habituated to.In the summer of 1931, T.H. Harrisson and J.A. Moy-Thomas visited St Kilda and reported in January 1932’s Nature publication that the house mouse had become extremely rare. They found it in only two of the recently vacated households where perishable food supplies had been left behind during the final 1930 evacuation. The 1931 visit indicated that some house mice were still surviving less than a year after the evacuation, especially in places where food remained. Published in the Journal of Zoology in 1969, a later assessment by R.J. Berry and B.J.K. Tricker concluded that the St Kilda house mouse became extinct within 18 months of the human population leaving in 1930.An early explanation for the extinction suggested that mice could no longer obtain enough food after the islanders left; but Berry and Tricker argued that competition with the field mouse was a more likely explanation. They suggested that the mere absence of humans was not sufficient to explain their extinction, as house mice can survive on uninhabited islands. The human departure, instead, stripped the house mice off their structural advantage, thus triggering a lethal survival competition that the wild field mice eventually won.The mouse population that was already established on St KildaThe disappearance of the human population in 1930 changed the field mouse’s relationship with the village buildings. The researchers suggested that the disappearance allowed the field mouse to enter a habitat that had previously been dominated by the house mouse.Apodemus sylvaticus hirtensis is a distinct St Kilda subspecies of the wood mouse and is larger than mainland forms. In a 1969 study of Apodemus sylvaticus populations across the Hebrides and Shetland, Berry argued that most of the island forms were unlikely remnants of prehistoric populations and were more probably introduced by humans. He suggested that Vikings or their descendants were the most likely agents.This is, however, a historical evolutionary interpretation rather than a documented record of exactly when the St Kilda population arrived. Today, the field mouse remains part of St Kilda’s ecosystem. As per the National Trust for Scotland, it is still common in Hirta and is also present on Dun, where it reportedly feeds on snails, insects, moss and seeds.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Police action was delayed, everything was visible in video’: Gurgaon biker Sia after accused arrest
articles.summary: GURGAON: Victim Sia, whose two-wheeler was allegedly hit by a car on Golf Course Road on Sunday, said she had posted a video of the incident the same .
articles.body: GURGAON: Victim Sia, whose two-wheeler was allegedly hit by a car on Golf Course Road on Sunday, said she had posted a video of the incident the same night and alleged that police action was delayed despite the footage being widely broadcast on news channels.“The incident took place on Sunday morning and I posted the video same night. The video was played widely on news channels but I believe (police) action was delayed. Everything was visible in the video, that how he hit me intentionally, " Sia told news agency PTI.“It is not a matter of male or female, there are several males with such bad mentality. They take somethings on their ego and then take steps like this person did. They were chasing, harassing me and asked me to stop. But when I didn't stop, they hit me and fled,” she said.Meanwhile, Kalyan Bainsla, the car driver accused of hitting Sia, was arrested from Rajgarh in Rajasthan on Tuesday, police said.The arrest came two days after his speeding car allegedly rammed into her Aprilia RS 457, sending her skidding on the road.Haryana State Women Commission chairperson Usha Priyadarshini said the commission took immediate cognisance of the incident and spoke to the police and the victim."The Commission took immediate cognisance of the matter. We spoke to the SHO of Sector 55-56 Police Station and later to ACP Amit Bhatia. By then, details of the incident had emerged. The video clearly showed a young man stalking the girl, "Haryana State Women Commission Chairperson Usha Priyadarshini told news agency ANI.She said the video showed the accused stalking the woman and alleged that he had been harassing her for some time."I also spoke to her personally, and she informed me that the accused had been stalking and harassing her for some time... This is a serious hit-and-run case on Golf Course Road. We have taken the matter very seriously, and the police have initiated action... The police have registered a case under Section 307 (attempt to murder). The accused, identified as Kalyan Baisla from Palwal, has been apprehended and arrested. We have instructed the police to ensure the safety of our daughters and sisters so that such incidents do not happen in the future, " she added.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Nato jets shoot down drone in Lithuanian airspace after Rutte warns Russia against strikes near alliance territory
articles.summary: Europe News: NEW DELHI: Nato fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight, officials said Tuesday, in an incident that came less than .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nato fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight, officials said Tuesday, in an incident that came less than a day after Nato Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned that strikes close to alliance territory would push the bloc to step up support for Ukraine.The drone was shot down near the village of Pratkūnai in the Kaišiadorys district, about 100 km west of Vilnius and near the Kaunas Reservoir, Lithuania’s National Crisis Management Center said.Lithuania’s military said it was the first time a drone had been shot down in the country’s airspace. Authorities did not disclose the drone’s origin or purpose, saying the incident remains under investigation.The incursion came shortly after Rutte, speaking at Nato headquarters in Brussels on Monday, said strikes “close to NATO territory” demonstrated Russian President Vladimir Putin’s “desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror.”“Russia is growing increasingly reckless as it continues its terrible war against Ukraine,” Rutte said. He also pledged to strengthen the 32-member alliance’s defences along its eastern border with Russia.Drone ‘likely’ carrying explosivesDrone incursions have repeatedly raised security concerns in Lithuania, which borders Belarus, a close Russian ally, and Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave.Antanas Matutis, commander of the Lithuanian air force, said wreckage from the drone had been recovered and that it “likely” was carrying explosives.Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania’s crisis management centre, told public broadcaster LRT that the drone most likely entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. It remained in the country for about 30 minutes and flew along the outskirts of populated areas before being intercepted, he said.Kyiv says it is ‘ready to support de-escalation’The incident came as Russian drone strikes continued across Ukraine, following a social media post by US President Donald Trump on Monday claiming Russia and Ukraine had agreed “not to hit” each other’s energy infrastructure.Trump provided no further details about the purported agreement, while Russia did not immediately comment. Previous attempts to broker even limited ceasefires have repeatedly collapsed, with Moscow and Kyiv accusing each other of violations.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said late Monday that Kyiv was “ready to support de-escalation.”“We see that the Russians feel the pressure from our precise strikes on Russia’s war economy. And so far, no one has seen any genuine desire on Russia’s part to move toward ending the war,” he said. “But if our American partners can ensure that Russia is genuinely ready to stop this war aimed at destroying life — and to do so for real and for the long term — Ukraine will take its own de-escalatory steps.”Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Tuesday that eight people were wounded in Russian strikes on Kyiv since the start of the day, including two people injured in strikes on gas stations in the capital.Meanwhile, Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces shot down 222 Ukrainian drones overnight.In the Russian city of Taganrog, a “massive” Ukrainian drone attack sparked several fires, regional Governor Yuri Slyusar said. He said two apartment buildings and three private homes were damaged, along with an educational institution, agricultural warehouses and a site belonging to Russian e-commerce company Ozon.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ohio wants to add 118 acres around a rare wetland to a nature preserve; if funding comes through, the protected habitat could grow to 450 acres and the family has offered to donate its house and 3 more acres
articles.summary: US News: A conservation effort in Ross County, Ohio, could significantly expand protection around a rare wetland complex if funding is secured for a proposed 1.
articles.body: A conservation effort in Ross County, Ohio, could significantly expand protection around a rare wetland complex if funding is secured for a proposed 118-acre land acquisition. The Ross County Park District is seeking to acquire the property, which would provide a buffer around the Kinnikinnick Fen and Herron Downs nature preserve properties as well as Kinnikinnick Creek. According to the Scioto Valley Guardian, which obtained the information from the Ross County Board of Commissioners, Ross County commissioners voted on September 8 to formally support the acquisition. If the project receives funding through Ohio’s Clean Ohio program, the preserved habitat could eventually grow to an estimated 450 acres. The property’s owners have also offered to donate their house and about three surrounding acres to the park district.Proposed acquisition would expand wetland protectionThe proposed acquisition would add 118 acres to the conservation landscape surrounding the existing Kinnikinnick Fen and Herron Downs properties. Rather than simply adding another isolated parcel of protected land, the acquisition would create a larger buffer around the wetland areas and Kinnikinnick Creek. That additional land could be important because wetlands are closely connected to the surrounding landscape. Water movement through adjoining properties can influence the condition of a wetland, while vegetation around waterways can provide additional protection for habitats and help maintain the character of the broader ecosystem.An initial environmental assessment of the property found a significant water flow path that feeds the wetland at Herron Downs. That finding has added to the conservation value of the proposed acquisition, as protecting the land around a wetland can also help safeguard the natural processes that support it. If funding is approved, the Ross County Park District would acquire the property and add it to the protected landscape.Funding remains key to the expansionThe proposed purchase is dependent on receiving financial support through Ohio’s Clean Ohio program. The county commissioners’ formal endorsement is intended to support the park district’s application as it seeks funding for the acquisition. The project would expand a conservation area that already includes the Kinnikinnick Fen and Herron Downs nature preserve properties. With the additional 118 acres, the total preserved habitat could reach approximately 450 acres.For the park district, the acquisition would therefore represent more than the preservation of a single parcel. It would strengthen the larger conservation area around the wetlands and creek while helping protect land connected to the existing natural areas. The environmental assessment’s identification of a significant water flow path is particularly relevant because changes to land surrounding wetlands can affect water movement and habitat conditions. Protecting the property could help maintain those connections over the long term.Family offers additional land and houseThe property also comes with an unusual offer from the Herron family. If the acquisition moves forward with Clean Ohio funding, the family has offered to donate the house located on the property, along with approximately three acres surrounding it, to the Ross County Park District. That means the conservation effort could ultimately involve more than the 118-acre acquisition itself. The additional three-acre donation would become part of the park district’s holdings, while the house would also be transferred to the organisation.The offer reflects the family’s willingness to support the broader conservation effort while allowing the property to become part of a larger protected landscape. The house and surrounding acreage would also become part of the park district’s holdings, although the immediate focus remains on securing funding for the proposed acquisition.Protecting a connected wetland landscapeThe planned expansion highlights why conservation groups often seek to protect land surrounding sensitive habitats rather than focusing only on the central wetland itself. Wetlands depend on surrounding hydrology, vegetation and drainage patterns. A property that contains a water flow path feeding an existing wetland can therefore have conservation value even when it is not itself entirely covered by wetland habitat.In this case, the proposed 118 acres would provide a buffer between the existing protected areas and surrounding land. Protecting that buffer could help maintain the ecological setting around Kinnikinnick Fen, Herron Downs and Kinnikinnick Creek. The potential 450-acre protected landscape would also create a larger area for conservation. Such additions can make it easier for land managers to protect habitats as a connected system rather than managing individual parcels separately.A larger conservation opportunity for Ross CountyThe commissioners’ support is an important step, but the expansion is not yet guaranteed. The Ross County Park District must still secure funding through the Clean Ohio program before the proposed acquisition can proceed. If that funding comes through, the project would give the county a significantly larger protected wetland landscape while adding another layer of protection around Kinnikinnick Creek and the water system feeding Herron Downs.The Herron family’s offer to donate the house and three additional acres would further strengthen the project. Together, the proposed acquisition and donation could turn the 118-acre property into an important addition to the region’s conservation network. For Ross County, the effort is ultimately about protecting more than a rare wetland itself. By securing the surrounding land and the water pathway connected to it, officials and the park district are seeking to expand protection around the wetland.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Such gimmicks are nothing new’: India slams Pakistan over 'phoney announcement' of Rs 70 lakh bounty on Masood Azhar
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday criticised Pakistan over its announcement of a PKR 70 lakh reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of J.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday criticised Pakistan over its announcement of a PKR 70 lakh reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar, calling it a “phoney” move and asking Islamabad to take concrete action against the terror group chief.Responding to Pakistan maintaining the bounty on Azhar, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Islamabad's announcement was unlikely to have any consequence."Such gimmicks and attempts at hoodwinking people by Pakistan are nothing new. We have seen similar gimmicks in the past as well. For a state sponsor of terrorism to make such phoney announcements—we all know how hollow they are. Pakistan must take concrete action rather than make announcements that are ultimately of no consequence..."Pakistan has continued to list Azhar in the Federal Investigation Agency's (FIA) “Red Book” of most-wanted terrorists and has retained a reward of PKR 70 Lakh for information leading to his apprehension or conviction.Azhar, the founder and chief of JeM, is wanted in India in connection with several terror cases, including the 2001 Parliament attack. India has also linked JeM to the 2016 Pathankot airbase attack and the 2019 Pulwama bombing.His name was first included in the FIA's Red Book in 2021 and has been retained in its 2026 edition. He is listed at serial number 1480 among 1,804 most-wanted terrorists.The FIA entry identifies Azhar as the head of Jaish-e-Mohammad and says the reward of up to PKR 70 lakh is for information leading directly to his “apprehension or conviction”.The cases cited against him in the FIA list were registered in Gujranwala, Multan and Lahore under provisions of Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act.India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar. Islamabad has maintained that he fled to Afghanistan, a claim rejected by Afghanistan's Taliban government.Azhar was among the fugitives India sought from Pakistan following the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, in which 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists killed 166 people.The latest development comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force's next plenary in Paris from October 26 to 30. Pakistan was placed on the FATF's increased monitoring list, commonly known as the grey list, in 2018 and remained there until 2022.It was removed after completing commitments under two FATF action plans focused on strengthening its anti-money laundering and counter-terror financing framework and implementing targeted financial sanctions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan military jets strike Kalat in fresh Balochistan attacks: Report
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistani military aircraft reportedly carried out airstrikes at two locations in Kalat on Monday, a day after a drone allegedly targeted a vehicle in.
articles.body: Pakistani military aircraft reportedly carried out airstrikes at two locations in Kalat on Monday, a day after a drone allegedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP).A jet aircraft reportedly conducted an airstrike in the Chappar area of Kalat, where a powerful blast was heard. There was no immediate information about casualties or the extent of damage.Another explosion was reported near Took and Dasht-e-Goran. The exact location of the blast could not immediately be confirmed, though jet aircraft were reportedly seen flying over the area around the time of the explosion, news agency ANI cited.Drone, helicopter attacks also reportedOn Sunday, a drone reportedly targeted a vehicle in Manguchar. Gunship helicopters also allegedly shelled Rudeenjo and nearby areas for several hours on Sunday, while quadcopter attacks were reported from parts of the district.Communication disruptions and movement restrictions in the affected areas have made it difficult to independently verify the reports or obtain comprehensive details about casualties and damage, TBP said.The reported attacks come amid a series of military operations and aerial strikes across Balochistan in recent weeks, with several incidents triggering allegations of civilian casualties.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: FBI director Kash Patel to face Senate panel over leadership, spending, and 2020 election probe
articles.summary: US News: FBI Director Kash Patel faces Senate Judiciary Committee questioning regarding leadership, taxpayer spending, and the investigation into the 2020 election. With bipartisan scrutiny, Patel's tenure is under fire as he defends his record amidst controversies and criticisms.
articles.body: FBI Director Kash Patel is scheduled to face senators on Tuesdayas the Senate Judiciary Committee questions him over his leadership of the bureau, use of taxpayer-funded resources and investigations stemming from the 2020 presidential election, according to Reuters.It will be Patel’s first appearance before the Senate since May. Democrats are expected to press him on several controversies surrounding his tenure, including claims about his conduct and questions over FBI spending.Republicans on the committee are expected to focus on the federal investigation into efforts to overturn the 2020 election. Chairman Chuck Grassley has identified the investigation as a priority for the committee.Patel is also likely to face questions about the recent resignation of Joe DiGenova, who had been leading a probe into several of Donald Trump’s political opponents. DiGenova abruptly stepped down last week from the investigation, which had sought to establish that Trump was the victim of a criminal conspiracy.Questions over Patel’s use of government resources have also drawn bipartisan scrutiny. Grassley asked in a May 5 letter for information about the FBI director’s use of a government aircraft, luxury vehicles and other taxpayer-funded expenses.Patel has faced other criticism during his time as FBI director. In May, he denied a media report alleging that excessive drinking had affected his ability to lead the agency.He has also attracted attention over reports of him scuba diving at a Pearl Harbor memorial and drinking beer while celebrating with the US men’s hockey team during the Milan Winter Olympics.Another potential issue is the FBI’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation. Recently released messages showed Patel directing a senior aide to respond to anonymous social media accounts that mocked the bureau’s efforts.The hearing could also bring scrutiny of Patel’s push to expand cooperation with China and Russia on transnational crime. Reuters previously reported that critics have argued that closer law-enforcement ties with the two countries could pose national security risks.Patel has defended his record by pointing to falling violent crime levels across the US. He has appeared with President Donald Trump to promote the decline, although the reduction began before Trump’s second term.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
